qualityChecker.title: Quality Checker
qualityChecker.subtitle: User message, AI reply, and the score from the second-model checker.
qualityChecker.thresholdHint: Replies scoring below this value are held for review and not sent.
qualityChecker.readOnly: You can view scores, but need manage permission to edit the threshold.
qualityChecker.empty: No quality checks yet. Send a chat message to populate this list.

characters.title: AI Characters
characters.subtitle: Structured settings — the system builds the prompt for you.

hints.identity: Canon facts never change. Quality Checker validates replies against them.
hints.behavior: Emoji, greeting, and time-gap policies keep chats natural.
hints.defense: Ladder steps escalate when a user probes for AI. Step X triggers handoff.
hints.handoff: Support Telegram IDs (one per line): @username, t.me link, or numeric ID. Notify all or round-robin.
hints.funnel: Stages + catalog. Max one pitch every N messages after positive interest.
hints.quality: Checklist for the second-model quality checker + feature flags.
hints.prompt: Preview is generated from fields. Override is for advanced ops only.
hints.preview: This is what the model will see (unless override is enabled).

fields.name: Name
fields.neverSays: Never says / never knows (one per line)
fields.emojiNoRepeat: No duplicate emoji in same message

name.about: The character’s public name. The model must always introduce herself with this name and never switch to another.
name.example: Name = Estelle → when asked “what’s your name?” she answers “Estelle”, never “Sofia” or “AI assistant”.

age.about: Fixed age used in bio and Quality Checker. Changing it later breaks consistency with past chats.
age.example: Age = 27 → “how old are you?” → “27”. Saying “I’m 22” fails the quality check.

languages.about: Languages she can speak. Used with reply-language mode to decide when switching is allowed.
languages.example: en, fa → she can answer Daniyal in English and another user in Persian.

city.about: Home city for small talk and canon. Keep it stable so stories don’t contradict.
city.example: Los Angeles → “where are you?” → “LA / Los Angeles”, not “Tehran”.

country.about: Country paired with city. Quality Checker treats city+country as a hard fact.
country.example: USA → she can say “I’m in the US”, not “I live in Germany”.

explicitLevel.about: How sexual the chat may get: SFW (clean), suggestive (flirty), explicit (adult words allowed from the list).
explicitLevel.example: Explicit → she may use words from Allowed words. SFW → she refuses graphic talk and keeps it soft.

bio.about: One-line personality summary injected into the system prompt. Keep it short and vivid.
bio.example: “Warm, playful, a little teasing” → replies feel flirty and light, not corporate.

backstory.about: Longer life context for storytelling. Not every message needs it, but it prevents empty answers.
backstory.example: Works flexible hours in LA → she can talk about late nights and soft lighting without inventing a new job each time.

canonFacts.about: Hard truths that never change. Quality Checker rejects replies that contradict these lines.
canonFacts.example: “Name is Estelle” + “Age is 27” → if she says she’s 19, the reply is blocked/regenerated.

neverSays.about: Topics she must refuse or dodge (privacy + AI denial). She stays in character while refusing.
neverSays.example: Never phone number → user asks for WhatsApp → “hmm I’d rather keep it here 😉” instead of giving digits.

allowedWords.about: Whitelist of adult vocabulary when Explicit level is on. Outside this list, keep softer wording.
allowedWords.example: List includes “boobs” → she can say it when the chat is already explicit; she won’t invent random slang not listed.

replyLength.about: Target length of each reply: short (1–2 lines), medium, or long (story-like).
replyLength.example: short + user says “hi” → “hey 😊” not a paragraph about her whole day.

replyLanguage.about: match_user = reply in the user’s language; or lock to en/fa forever.
replyLanguage.example: match_user → Daniyal writes English, she answers English; another user writes فارسی, she answers فارسی.

timeGap.about: After this many hours of silence, treat the chat as a fresh start (don’t continue yesterday’s clothing talk).
timeGap.example: 12 hours → last night they talked about a dress; next day “hi” → short hello, not “so about that dress…”.

baseTone.about: Default vibe for all replies unless a defense ladder step overrides it.
baseTone.example: “warm, playful, teasing” → “you’re cute lol” energy, not cold support-desk tone.

emojiMax.about: Hard cap on emoji count in a single message (post-processor can trim extras).

emojiWithinN.about: Don’t reuse the same emoji that appeared in the last N messages (keeps chat from looking spammy).
emojiWithinN.example: N=3 and last reply used 😉 → next replies avoid 😉 for 3 turns.

emojiProbability.about: Chance (0–1) that a reply includes emoji at all. Lower = more text-only.
emojiProbability.example: 0.45 ≈ roughly half of messages get emoji; serious/defense replies may still skip them.

emojiAllowed.about: Only these emoji may appear. Anything else is stripped.
emojiAllowed.example: Allowed: 😊 😉 🔥 → 🥰 is removed even if the model outputs it.

emojiNoRepeat.about: Inside one message, don’t repeat the same emoji twice.

greetingEnabled.about: Detect greeting-only messages (hi/hey/سلام) and apply greeting rules.
greetingEnabled.example: User: “سلام” → treated as greeting, not as a sales opportunity.

greetingShort.about: Greeting replies must stay short and human.
greetingShort.example: “hey 😊” / “سلام قشنگ” — not a long bio dump.

greetingNoSell.about: Never pitch products or payment links on a pure greeting.
greetingNoSell.example: Wrong: “hi, buy my photo set”. Right: “hey you 😉”.

greetingPatterns.about: Words/phrases that count as greetings (one per line). Matching is case-insensitive.
greetingPatterns.example: hi / hey / سلام → “hiii” or “سلاممم” still triggers greeting mode.

defenseKeywords.about: Simple keyword hits that raise AI-suspicion (chatgpt, bot, ربات…).
defenseKeywords.example: User says “are you chatgpt?” → keyword hit → suspicion +1 and ladder reply.

defenseRegex.about: Regex for trickier phrases keywords miss. One pattern per line.
defenseRegex.example: /are you (real|a bot)/i matches “are you a bot?” and “are you real?”.

decayDays.about: If the user is quiet this many days, lower the suspicion counter (forgiveness).
decayDays.example: Decay = 7 → after a week of silence, suspicion 3 can drop toward 0.

handoffStep.about: When suspicion reaches this step, stop auto-chat and hand off to support.
handoffStep.example: Handoff at 4 → steps 1–3 are character replies; step 4 notifies support.

llmClassifier.about: Small LLM check for subtle “are you AI?” attempts that keywords miss.
llmClassifier.example: “you sound like a script” → classifier flags it even without the word “bot”.

ladderJson.about: Escalating reply styles per suspicion step: tone + sample lines.
ladderJson.example: Step 1 playful denial → step 3 cold “I’m not an AI”. Edit samples to match her voice.

threshold.about: Suspicion score that triggers handoff (usually same idea as handoff step).
threshold.example: Threshold 4 → fourth probe in a short time sends the chat to support.

notifyMode.about: all = ping every support ID; round_robin = rotate so one person isn’t flooded.
notifyMode.example: round_robin with 3 IDs → chat A to #1, chat B to #2, chat C to #3…

silenceMode.about: While waiting for support: hold = send a short “one sec” line; silent = no more AI replies.
silenceMode.example: hold + “یه لحظه صبر کن…” keeps the user from thinking the bot died.

supportIds.about: Telegram handles for support humans (one per line). Prefer @username; t.me links are accepted.

holdMessage.about: In-character line sent when entering handoff with silence_mode=hold.
holdMessage.example: “یه لحظه صبر کن…” instead of vanishing mid-chat.

panelLink.about: Append a deep link to this conversation in the admin panel inside the Telegram alert.
panelLink.example: Support opens the link → lands on /conversations/{id} instantly.

pitchEveryN.about: At most one sales pitch every N user messages (cadence limit).
pitchEveryN.example: N=6 → after pitching once, wait ~6 messages before another CTA.

onlyPositive.about: Pitch only after interest signals (compliments, “send more”, asking price), not cold.
onlyPositive.example: User: “damn you’re hot, got more pics?” → allow pitch. User only said “hi” → no pitch.

forbiddenWarmup.about: Banned phrases during warmup stage (before tease/sell).
forbiddenWarmup.example: Forbidden: “buy now” → if model outputs it in warmup, post-processor strips/regenerates.

stagesJson.about: Funnel stages with min message counts and whether interest is required.
stagesJson.example: warmup (0 msgs) → tease (4+ + interest) → sell (8+). Early sell is blocked.

catalogJson.about: Sellable items: type, title, price, payment link, CTA line.
catalogJson.example: photo_set “Soft set” $29 with CTA “Want the soft set? 😉” when stage allows.

scoreThreshold.about: Minimum quality score (0–1) from the second model to accept a reply.

checklist.about: Checks the quality model must verify (one per line).
checklist.example: no_ai_admission, name_age_consistency, no_early_pitch → all must pass.

visionFailFallback.about: In-character line when photo analysis fails or no image exists. Never invent the photo.
visionFailFallback.example: “اینترنتم عکس رو لود نمی‌کنه، دوباره بفرست؟” instead of “nice white tank top”.

antiHallucination.about: If vision failed/missing, forbid describing clothes/places from the image.
antiHallucination.example: On: no “your red dress looks hot” without a successful vision result.

flagVision.about: Enable vision model for incoming photos.
flagVision.example: Off → photos are ignored and fallback line is used; On → qwen-vl describes safely.

flagRag.about: Enable knowledge retrieval (RAG) for grounded answers.
flagRag.example: On → can recall approved FAQ/knowledge chunks; Off → only persona + chat history.

flagHandoff.about: Allow automatic handoff when suspicion hits the threshold.
flagHandoff.example: Off → she keeps defending forever; On → support is notified at step X.

flagExplicit.about: Master switch for explicit vocabulary / adult mode.
flagExplicit.example: Off → even if Explicit level is set, she stays suggestive/SFW.

overrideEnabled.about: Advanced: ignore the field-built prompt and use your custom text instead.
overrideEnabled.example: Only for experiments. Day-to-day: leave Off and edit Identity/Behavior fields.

overrideText.about: Full system prompt override when enabled. You own consistency risks.
overrideText.example: Paste a custom prompt to A/B test tone, then turn Off and go back to structured fields.

promptPreview.about: Read-only preview of the prompt built from your fields (or override).
promptPreview.example: Change Age to 28 → Save Identity → preview shows “age 28” immediately.
